transformation: Rename columns to clear, consistent names
why_it_was_needed: Original names such as 'adr' or 'stays_in_week_nights' are cryptic or long; clear names make later analysis code readable.
Duplicate bookings inflate counts and revenue and leak identical rows between train and test sets in ML.

transformation: Standardise text (trim spaces, lower case, ISO codes upper)
why_it_was_needed: Mixed case or stray spaces create fake categories ('City Hotel' vs 'city hotel').

transformation: Convert dates (build arrival_date, parse status date)
why_it_was_needed: Year, month name and day were in 3 separate columns; a real datetime enables sorting, monthly grouping and time-series work.
Default int64 wastes memory; correct types also document that flags are binary and counts are whole numbers.
You cannot fix what you have not measured; some missing data is hidden behind text like 'Undefined'.
Dataset documentation says meal 'Undefined' equals 'SC' (no meal package); the others become an explicit 'unknown' category.
Over 90% empty - imputing would invent data. The useful signal (booked through a company or not) is kept as a 0/1 flag.

transformation: Fill missing 'agent' with 0 and add has_agent flag
why_it_was_needed: A missing agent id means the guest booked directly; 0 = no agent.
Only a few rows are missing and the vast majority of bookings have no children, so 0 is the safest imputation.
Guessing a country (e.g. the most common) would bias country-wise analysis; an explicit unknown label is honest.
A booking for nobody is a data-entry error and breaks per-guest metrics.
A stay with no nights has no revenue and no duration - invalid for length-of-stay and revenue analysis.
A room price cannot be negative. (A rate of exactly 0 is kept - these are genuine complimentary stays.)

transformation: Detect outliers with the IQR rule (1.5 x IQR fences)
why_it_was_needed: Extreme values (e.g. a 5,400 room rate, 55 adults) distort means and hurt ML models; we first measure how many there are.

transformation: Cap extreme outliers (winsorise) instead of deleting rows
why_it_was_needed: Capping keeps the booking but removes the distortion. Skewed count columns use percentile caps because their IQR is 0.
Raw data only has parts; totals and revenue are what analysts actually report on.
Binning continuous values makes patterns easy to compare and gives models stable categorical features.
Hotel demand is highly seasonal; these allow monthly and seasonal reports.
A single behavioural segment is easier to analyse than three separate guest-count columns.
Whether the guest got a different room than booked is a known driver of cancellations and complaints.
Time order is needed for time-series and time-based train/test splits; booking_id gives every row a unique key.

transformation: Final validation checks (nulls, duplicates, ranges, size)
why_it_was_needed: Proves the output really is analysis-ready before it is saved.
details: all checks passed; final shape 86,638 x 46
